neighbours.label: The punctuation right before a parenthesised item in a running pattern of such items, i.e. predicting the next '(' entry: ';' before '(2)' in a '(1) ...; (2) ...' list, ':' before a '(xxx)' area code in a contact list. Quiet when the same list uses numbering without parentheses.
fire: Ratings were recorded as: (1) poor; (2) fair; (3) good; (4) excellent.
Steps: (a) wash the jar; (b) dry it; (c) fill it with sugar.
Each patient chose one option: (1) surgery; (2) medication; (3) waiting.
Reach us at Main: (206) 555-0110 or Billing: (206) 555-0111.
Options include: (i) leasing; (ii) buying outright; (iii) renting monthly.
Pain was scored as follows: (0) none; (1) mild; (2) severe.
quiet: Ratings were recorded as poor, fair, good or excellent by each rater.
Steps: wash the jar, then dry it, then fill it with sugar and close it.
Each patient chose one option, either surgery, medication or waiting.
Reach us at the main office or by email if billing has a question.
Options include leasing, buying outright or renting on a monthly basis.
Pain was scored as none, mild or severe by the nurse on duty.
Our branches are in Denver and Boulder and open at nine each day.

predictions: median fire ~0.5 (probes: '(1) never; (2)' 0.91, 'Tel: (415) ... Fax: (415)' 0.87, 'et al. (2010)' 0.37); near misses < 0.2 (copyright policy 0.01, send a fax 0.14). Card flags broad (2.3%), so near misses may fire weakly.
short: punctuation before the next '(' item in a pattern
notes: Card peaks: ' Copyright' before (C), ':param' before (list), 'and' before (iii), 'et al.' before (2009), ';' before (2). The pole sits on the token before '(', so it must predict it; near misses keep the same list content but drop the parentheses, so no '(' is predictable.
